sources.name: UK general election 2024: results by constituency
sources.publisher: House of Commons Library / UK Parliament
sources.note: Every candidate's votes in all 650 seats. We group them by party (Workers Party and small parties go into 'Other parties').

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2024 general election
sources.note: 42,119 adults polled 5–8 July 2024. Gives the vote share of each party by age, sex, social grade and education, and how big each group was among voters.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2024 election
sources.note: 17,394 adults, 5–8 July 2024. Our source for how White, Asian, Black and Mixed voters split (Ipsos warns the minority sub-group samples are small), plus turnout estimates for the fun facts, e.g. only 37% of 18–24s.

sources.name: Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021
sources.note: Population by ethnic group (White 81.7%, Asian 9.3%, Black 4.0%, Mixed 2.9%, Other 2.1%). Combined with Ipsos turnout to size each group among voters.

sources.name: EU referendum results
sources.note: Remain 48.1%, Leave 51.9%. Used as a rough guide to how many 2024 voters were Remainers vs Leavers (people who didn't vote in 2016 are folded in).

sources.name: One in five voters say they are voting tactically at the 2024 general election
sources.note: Matthew Smith, 1 July 2024. 22% of voters said they were voting tactically (39% of Lib Dem voters, 29% of Labour voters, 8-12% for Con, Reform and Green). If nobody voted tactically, YouGov's implied shares were Labour 29% (8 points lower), Lib Dems about 12% (2 lower) and Greens 13% (6 higher), with little change for the Conservatives and Reform. We use these net changes for the 'Undo tactical voting' switch under PR.

sources.name: The Liberal Democrats in 2024: vote efficiency and tactical voting
sources.note: Griffiths, Green and Fieldhouse, 5 September 2024. Shows 44% of 2019 Labour voters switched to the Lib Dems where the Lib Dems were the main challenger to the Conservatives. Background on where tactical voting happened; not used in the numbers.

sources.name: Who's tactically voting, and why?
sources.note: Connor Ibbetson, 10 December 2019. 19% of voters said they were voting tactically (36% of Lib Dem first-choice voters, 19% of Labour, 12% of Conservative). It doesn't say where those votes would otherwise go, so we leave the tactical switch off for 2019.

sources.name: Half of us: turnout patterns at the 2024 general election
sources.note: Background on who didn't vote: just 52.8% of the voting-age population turned out.

sources.name: UK general election results 2010–2019
sources.publisher: House of Commons Library / UK Parliament
sources.note: Every candidate's votes in every seat at the 2010, 2015, 2017 and 2019 general elections.

sources.name: How Britain voted in 2010
sources.note: 10,211 adults over the campaign. Con/Lab/LD/Other shares and turnout by sex, age, class, housing and ethnicity, plus group sizes.

sources.name: How Britain voted in 2015
sources.note: 9,149 adults. Con/Lab/LD/UKIP/Green shares and turnout by sex, age, class, housing and ethnicity. Group sizes estimated from Ipsos's 2010 profile.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2017 election
sources.note: 7,505 adults. We use it for housing and ethnicity (Con/Lab/LD/UKIP/Other) and turnout.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2019 election
sources.note: 27,951 adults. We use it for housing and ethnicity (Con/Lab/LD/Other) and turnout.

sources.name: How Britain voted at the 2017 general election
sources.note: 52,615 adults. Full party shares and turnout by age, sex, social grade, education, work and the newspaper people read.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2019 general election
sources.note: 41,995 adults. Full party shares by age, sex, social grade, education, work, income and Brexit vote. No turnout, so group sizes use YouGov's 2017 turnout.

sources.name: Ethnicity and national identity in England and Wales: 2011
sources.note: 86% of people identified as White in 2011. Used with Ipsos turnout to size ethnic groups among voters, 2010–2019.

sources.name: 2024 General Election Census constituency summaries
sources.publisher: Ralph Scott (from ONS / Nomis and Scotland's Census, Census 2021)
sources.note: Census 2021 for all 632 GB seats on the 2024 boundaries. We use it to give each 2024 seat its own mix of ages, sexes, social grades, education, housing, work and ethnicity.

sources.name: parlitools: Census 2011 by constituency
sources.publisher: Evan Odell (from ONS and Scotland's Census, Census 2011)
sources.note: Census 2011 for all 632 GB seats on the 2010–2019 boundaries. Gives each 2010–2019 seat its own local mix.

sources.name: UK hex maps (constituencies 2010–2023 and local authorities 2021)
sources.note: Hex layouts for the maps: one hexagon per seat or council, so every area is the same size.

sources.name: EU referendum results by counting area
sources.note: Remain and Leave votes in all 382 counting areas (Remain 16,141,241; Leave 17,410,742).

sources.name: How Britain voted (EU referendum)
sources.note: 5,455 adults on 23–24 June 2016. Remain/Leave split and each group's share of voters by age, sex, social grade, education, income and 2015 vote.

sources.name: How the United Kingdom voted on Thursday… and why
sources.note: 12,369 referendum voters. Our source for housing and ethnicity.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2016 EU referendum
sources.note: Turnout estimates by group, e.g. 53% of 18–24s.

sources.name: Scottish independence referendum: results by council area
sources.note: Yes and No votes in all 32 council areas (Yes 1,617,989; No 2,001,926).

sources.name: How Scotland voted, and why
sources.note: 2,046 referendum voters. Yes/No by age (including 16–17s), sex, social grade and Westminster vote.

sources.name: So how many 16 and 17 year olds voted?
sources.publisher: What Scotland Thinks (ICM for the Electoral Commission)
sources.note: Self-reported turnout by age, e.g. 75% of 16–17s.
